sql_readbacks.query:
WITH old AS (
 SELECT x->>'caller' AS caller,j.target AS target
 FROM public.lf_eventos e CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(e.payload->'sql_callers') x
 CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(x->'callees') j(target)
 WHERE e.id=20161
), now AS (
 SELECT n.nspname||'.'||p.proname AS caller,p.prosrc AS body
 FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=p.pronamespace
), comparisons AS (
 SELECT old.caller,old.target,
  n.body ILIKE '%'||old.target||'%' AS naive_substring,
  n.body ~ ('(^|[^[:alnum:]_])'||old.target||'[[:space:]]*\(') AS exact_call_token
 FROM old JOIN now n ON n.caller=old.caller
)
SELECT count(*) AS total_edges,
 count(*) FILTER(WHERE naive_substring) AS naive_retained,
 count(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT naive_substring) AS naive_missing,
 count(*) FILTER(WHERE exact_call_token) AS exact_call_retained,
 count(*) FILTER(WHERE NOT exact_call_token) AS exact_call_missing,
 count(*) FILTER(WHERE naive_substring AND NOT exact_call_token) AS substring_only
FROM comparisons
sql_readbacks.limits: Exact syntax regex is stronger than substring but may still match comments/strings or miss dynamic calls; not an AST and not runtime attestation.
